# Code of Conduct

We want the Pookie community to be a good place to hang out and ship things. That means being welcoming to people of every background, skill level, and identity, and treating each other like adults.

This applies everywhere the project lives: GitHub issues, pull requests, code reviews, Discord, social posts about the project, in-person meetups, and any other public or private channel where you're representing Pookie.

## Be decent

- Be kind. Default to assuming good intent.
- Be patient with people who are new, learning, or having a rough day.
- Disagree on ideas, not people. Critique the code, not the author.
- Give credit. If someone's idea or work helped you, say so.
- When you're wrong, say so. When someone else is wrong, help them get it right without making it personal.

## Don't be a jerk

The following are not okay, regardless of how funny you think the joke is:

- Harassment, intimidation, or sustained disruption.
- Personal attacks, insults, or demeaning comments. This includes attacks based on race, ethnicity, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability, neurotype, mental illness, physical appearance, body size, age, religion, or socioeconomic status.
- Sexualized language or imagery, or unwelcome sexual attention.
- Doxing or sharing someone's private information without permission.
- Threats of violence.
- Spam, off-topic self-promotion, or repeatedly derailing discussions.
- Advocating for or encouraging any of the above.

If you're not sure whether something crosses the line, it probably does. Ask first or skip it.

## Reporting

If you see something that violates this code, or if someone is making you uncomfortable, please tell us. You can:

- Email the maintainers privately (see GitHub for current maintainer contacts).
- DM a maintainer on [Discord](https://discord.gg/hUesQBQGUn).
- Open a private issue if you're comfortable doing so.

Reports will be handled confidentially. We won't share your identity with the person you're reporting without your consent, except where we're legally required to.

## Enforcement

Maintainers are responsible for enforcing this code. We can and will take action when needed, including:

1. A private warning, with an explanation of what was wrong.
2. A public warning.
3. A temporary ban from project spaces.
4. A permanent ban from project spaces.

Maintainers who violate this code in spirit or letter will face the same consequences. We're not above the rules.

## Scope

This code applies to everyone in project spaces and to anyone representing the project in public, including official social accounts, talks, or community events.

## Attribution

This document is loosely adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/) and the [Recurse Center social rules](https://www.recurse.com/manual#sub-sec-social-rules), which are both worth reading in full.
